papers.title: Superregular solitonic solutions of the defocusing nonlocal nonlinear Schrodinger equation and their novel perspectives
papers.abstract: Previous studies have indicated that the local defocusing nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation (NLSE) is modulationally stable. Therefore, superregular solitonic solutions characterizing the nonlinear evolution of modulational instability under weak localized perturbations do not exist. In this work, we study the nonlinear stage of the modulation instability of a condensate in the framework of the defocusing nonlocal NLSE. By using the dressing method and Joukowski transformation, we systematically derive the general $N$-solitonic solution of the defocusing nonlocal NLSE, and the explicit expressions for one-solitonic, two-solitonic and superregular two-solitonic solutions are provided. Then dynamics of these solutions is also examined. We find that these solutions show a much wider variety than those in the local NLSE, such as the one solitonic solution composed of two interacting wave components and the two-solitonic solution containing four wave components. Finally, the accuracy and noise robustness of the analytical solutions are confirmed by numerical simulations. Such results advance the theory of superregular solitonic solutions in nonlocal systems and offer new physical understanding of wave propagation in nonlocal nonlinear media.

papers.title: Synchronization transitions in ensembles of active particles with distance-dependent higher-order interactions
papers.abstract: Higher-order interactions are ubiquitous in biological systems and can be used to better describe the ensemble dynamics of self-propelled particles. To this end, this article investigates a Vicsek-Kuramoto model with distance-dependent higher-order interactions and obtains analytical results, albeit under certain assumptions, that characterize its collective dynamics. Subsequently, these are validated through simulations of the system equations, demonstrating both continuous and explosive transitions between the asynchronous and synchronous collective states. Further numerical results also reveal that short-range interactions and tightly clustered initial states can lead to deviations from the theoretical predictions, whereas the latter can be offset by increasing the common self-propulsion velocity. These results offer insights into a broad class of active matter systems with higher-order interactions, and provide a framework for designing and utilizing them for specific applications.

papers.title: Rheology and Velocity Distribution of Couette Flow for Protoplasmic Streaming
papers.abstract: We investigate two-dimensional Couette flow between parallel plates as a model of protoplasmic streaming in plant cells using a combined Langevin and Navier?Stokes simulation. The interaction between the fluid and biological materials is implemented using a Finsler geometry (FG) modeling technique, in which the interaction strength, represented by quantities such as relative viscosity, effectively varies with an internal degree of freedom (IDOF) associated with the biological materials. The simulations demonstrate that the Couette flow exhibits a linear velocity profile along the vertical direction perpendicular to the plates, as well as a peak structure in the velocity distribution consistent with reported experimental observations obtained by laser light scattering. The simulations also demonstrate that the model exhibits shear-thinning behavior typical of non-Newtonian fluids, with the viscosity minimized in the boundary region. Additionally, we find that the rheological properties are connected to the conformal transformation of the interaction between the fluid and the IDOF. Within the FG modeling framework, the conformally flat configuration of the IDOF, which is neither anisotropic nor randomly isotropic, is introduced as a minimum-energy state that characterizes the shear-thinning rheological properties of two-dimensional Couette flow.

papers.title: A Phase-Field Study of Desiccation Crack Pattern Maturation under Drying-Wetting Cycles
papers.abstract: The characteristic intersection angle of the desiccation crack relaxes from near \ang{90} toward \ang{120} under repeated drying--wetting cycles. However, the theoretical understanding of this relaxation is insufficient, especially the modeling of the drying--wetting cycles. Here we introduce a phase-field model of desiccation fracture, extending the model proposed in previous studies by adding crack healing and a scar effect left by past cracks. By repeating drying--wetting cycles in a finite element simulation, we find that the angle distribution develops a growing peak near \ang{120} as the cycle number increases, consistent with experiments. The standard deviation of the intersection angle from \ang{120} relaxes exponentially with a characteristic time of about 2.85 cycles. These results are consistent with experiments, except that the characteristic time is slightly smaller than the experimental value. Crack energy dominates the total energy and also relaxes exponentially with nearly the same characteristic cycle as the angle relaxation. This decay is driven mainly by a shortening of the effective crack length rather than a change in effective fracture toughness.
